# Research notes: how to sharpen a kitchen knife

Budget used: 8 searches, 5 page reads that loaded, plus 1 attempt that loaded nothing (PubMed's cookie wall). Nothing was paid for, no sign-in, no contact.

## Searches and what each gave

1. Science of Sharp burr formation, deburring, micrographs: the Science of Sharp burr series (2015, 2022, 2024, 2025). No peer-reviewed study of whetstone burrs turned up; the machining-burr papers are irrelevant. This led to the read of S1.
2. Honing steel, realigning a rolled edge, electron microscope: S2 ("steeling primarily produces a micro-bevel", realignment rare) and Wikipedia's burnishing account (S8). This is the surprise of the topic: the common line that a steel only realigns the edge is contested. Led to the read of S2.
3. Wüsthof and Zwilling factory angles: about 14-15 degrees for Western knives and about 10 for Japanese-style ones, but mostly through retailer charts and summaries; Wüsthof gives both 14 and 14.5.
4. Sharpness, cutting force and grip force in meat cutting: Karltun 2016 (upkeep skill outweighs steel), McGorry 2003 (citation only), a review with 15%/30% force increases in a gel (source not identified, so not used) and a poultry risk-score study (not used).
5. Whetstone method (burr, marker trick, angle, grits): no Serious Eats result; popular guides (S12). This led to the read of S4, the most detailed method page.
6. Pull-through damage under the microscope: one Science of Sharp study on S110V (S9, snippet) plus forum and magazine opinion. T3's evidence is thin.
7. Whether "a dull knife is more dangerous" has evidence: no injury data at all, only anecdote, a reader poll and a plausible mechanism (legend, C04).
8. Wüsthof's own angle page (wusthof.com only): found the FAQ (S6), the how-to page and the 14.5 product pages. This led to the read of S3.

## Reads

S1 and S2 were read in text and captions, but the micrographs did not render. S3 and S4 were read in full. For S5, PubMed refused the automated fetch, so I read the abstract through the Europe PMC record instead; the full text is paywalled.

## Dropped, and why

- **Coin-stack angle rule** ("two stacked coins give about 15 degrees", S4 and S12). The angle a lift gives depends on blade height. Raising the spine by h on a blade w tall tilts it by about arcsin(h/w), so two coins (about 3.5 mm) under a 5 cm chef's knife give about 4 degrees, not 15; 15 degrees needs about 13 mm. This is my own geometry, not a source, so I simply don't use the rule. The marker trick checks the real contact instead.
- **Thumbnail test** (S4) and the arm-hair test (other guides): a blade on skin or a nail reads as risky in a picture. Paper and the tomato are enough.
- **"A dull knife is more dangerous"**: no counts exist (legend), so the film leaves the saying out. The measured part (a duller edge needs more force, C03) may be said. Nothing about cuts or injuries is said or shown.
- **Holiday and superstition devices**: the maker's page had Thanksgiving and Black Friday banners, and "sharpen before the holiday roast" is a common hook. Both are holiday devices and are never used. Neither is any knife-gift superstition.
- **Wüsthof's "hand-wash after honing to remove excess steel"**: tempting as support for the metal-removal view, but it doesn't say whose steel, so it is not used as evidence.
- **"Burrs aren't always bad; toothy coarse edges can outperform"** (S1): a true nuance, but it muddies a beginner's step, so it is left out.
- **Electric and guided sharpeners**: no read evidence; they would belong to T3 only.
- **Meat-plant imagery**: S5 is told with aprons, knives and a chart. No meat, carcass or blood is shown.

## Where I was unsure

- S1 and S2 are one self-published author (credentials not stated on the pages; the about page wasn't opened). I trusted the methods (SEM, focused-ion-beam cross-sections) and the hedges he writes, not a CV. S2's blades were utility blades and an S30V knife, not kitchen knives.
- The burr signal (C13) is confirmed for the first side. The flipped-burr trap on the second side (C15) rests on one documented example, so it is said as "can", never "always". The advice to give side two its full share (M13) is my reasoning from that example.
- "Per side" for Wüsthof's 14 degrees is implied by the page's steps and stated only in the FAQ (snippet). The Western angle number genuinely differs between sources (C09), so the film names the maker's figure and the marker check, not one universal number.
- S5 was read as an abstract only (paraphrased by the fetch tool, with short verbatim quotes); effect sizes are unknown. Carrying it to home cooks is an inference (M20, hedged in B09).
- In the plan sketch I put `depends_on` inside `significance`, as the brief asked. The manual's beat map keeps `depends_on` on the beat itself, and the checks read it there, so it moves when this becomes beat-map.json.
